dedupe_keys.name: a comprehensive global database of tailings flows 63 tailings dam failures 1928 2020

description: This database documents 63 tailings flows, the downstream mass movements caused when tailings impoundments fail, from 1928 to 2020. The Borealis page says the authors screened more than 350 historical waste impoundment failures in earlier secondary datasets and kept those meeting strict case selection criteria, using satellite imagery, digital elevation models and published sources to report breach, outflow and runout properties in a consistent framework. Files include the supplementary database table, a README, a supplementary article and one satellite or aerial image or runout profile per event, for cases such as Stava, Aznalcollar, Ajka, Mount Polley, Fundao and Feijao. It supports the 2021 Engineering Geology paper by Rana, Ghahramani, Evans, McDougall, Small and Take, and was released on 14 July 2021 (version 2.1) as downloadable files, free under CC0 1.0, with global coverage. Caveats: the page says the data should be used only for screening-level assessments, analogue comparison and research, because site conditions strongly control post-breach behaviour. For simulation it gives magnitude-frequency statistics, outflow volumes and runout distances to set up tailings dam breach scenarios and to test runout and flood models that reach downstream roads, settlements and water intakes. Related catalogue records include the breach and runout characteristics database, the Global Tailings Portal, the WISE chronology of tailings dam failures and the Mount Polley breach review.

provider: Nahyan M. Rana and co-authors, via Borealis
